title_zh: 这场密室逃脱全靠脑筋急转弯
title_en: Chinese Humor (6/20): The Escape Room We Cracked with Brain-Teasers
note_en: Every riddle in this story is a real Chinese brain-teaser (脑筋急转弯): object riddles, number riddles and riddles about building characters from parts (王, 早, 合, 卡, 众, 森, 愁). It's told in the first person plural ("we"), a rare team-quest format for the series in which each riddle becomes its own obstacle.

sentences.en: But what nearly stumped us next was the simplest question in the whole escape room: "Which is heavier, a jin of iron or a jin of cotton?" One friend argued very seriously for a whole minute that the iron was heavier, until we reminded him that a jin is just a unit of weight, so a jin of iron and a jin of cotton weigh the same, of course.
